newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot aluminum premiums stable, alloy weakens.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot aluminum premiums stable, alloy weakens.

text.p: Aluminum premiums in the United States remain fairly stable on nearby shipments but tail off later in the year, while benchmark A380 alloy prices slide, putting further pressure on secondary smelter margins as scrap remains relatively expensive, dealers and merchants said.
Midwest premiums on Western grade metal were quoted at 4.75 to 5.25 cents per pound for June and July delivery, falling to 4.50 cents later in the year.
Dealers were taking a close interest in the U.S. Stockpile sale of 10,000 short tons of T-bar Wednesday.
Brown Industries bid for about half the metal on offer and, according to the prices the company offered, was likely to win this amount, dealers said. The outcome of the sale was due soon.
Merchants were trying to uncover details about Brown, which already bought a $9.5 million chunk of zinc from Stockpile last month and payment is due by June 21, dealers noted.
Monthly aluminum Stockpile sales will eventually dampen U.S. premiums if demand suffers any seasonal summer slowdown, one broker believed. "It would loosen up the situation further," a broker said.
Meanwhile aluminum scrap prices have failed to tumble as rapidly as alloy prices, putting more of a squeeze on secondary smelter margins, producer officials said.
The A380 Midwest alloy price has fallen from about 77 to 78 cents per pound earlier in the year to 74 to 74.5 cents.
